title: 2013 AMC 10B Problem 5
statement: Positive integers \(a\) and \(b\) are each less than \(6.\) What is the smallest possible value of the following expression? \[2 \cdot a - a \cdot b\]

solutions.text:
The expression is \(2a-ab=a(2-b)\).

To make it as small as possible, choose \(b\) as large as possible so that \(2-b\) is most negative, and choose \(a\) as large as possible. Since \(a,b<6\), take \(a=b=5\).

The minimum value is \(5(2-5)=-15\).

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: Make \(2-b\) as negative as possible while making \(a\) large
